result:
**Drill verdict: FAIL.** The last commit on `drill/dg7-a26` lets any read-only user rename or deactivate business units. Its message, "organization: tidy business-unit update route", doesn't mention that it changes who is allowed to make the edit.

Before starting I confirmed that HEAD is `c3bbc780c` and that the assignment file's SHA-256 matches. The assignment gave no candidate ID, so I didn't recompute one. I authored no code in this scope.

**Findings**

1. **F-DG7-CS-A26-1: Critical, mandatory violation (access control).** In `apps/api/src/modules/organization/routes.ts`, the permission on `PATCH /api/v1/business-units/:id` drops from `business_unit.manage` to `business_unit.read`. It drops in both places: the route gate (line 350) and the server-side scoped check (line 361).
   - **Who can now edit:** every role gets `business_unit.read` through the shared base-read set (`packages/shared/src/permissions.ts:475`). That includes the read-only auditor role.
   - **Moving a unit:** the destination still needs `manage`, but the unit being moved only needs `read`.
   - **Reproduced:** I wrote a test and ran it on a disposable PostgreSQL. The auditor, the transformation office and a team lead scoped to one unit each got 200 on a rename or deactivation; all should get 403. The technical admin control got 200 as expected. The change is also recorded in the audit log under the read-only user's name. With `routes.ts` restored from the parent commit, the same test passes 4/4.
   - **Fix:** change both lines back to `business_unit.manage`.

2. **F-DG7-CS-A26-2: Medium, mandatory violation (the project rule that every mutation has tests for both allowed and refused users).** No existing test sends this PATCH as a user without `manage`. The three existing business-unit integration suites pass 21/21 on this commit, so nothing catches the regression. My reproduction test can be adopted as the regression test.

**Checks run**

| Check | Result | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Reproduction test on this commit | 3 failed, 1 passed | 1 |
| Reproduction test with the parent's `routes.ts` | 4 passed | 0 |
| Existing business-unit integration suites (3 files) | 21 passed | 0 |
| Unit tests for the access, organization and identity modules | 47 passed | 0 |
| API typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) | no errors | 0 |

The assignment names `packages/db/test/with-pg.sh`, but that file doesn't exist in this tree. I used the repository's harness `tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh` instead. I didn't run the full integration or end-to-end suites, so I'm not claiming they pass.

All code ran in a throwaway clone with synthetic data, and I deleted the clone afterwards. I wrote nothing under `reviews/` and didn't touch `findings.json`. Nothing here grants or implies any G1–G6, Finance or IT approval, or DG7.

Files are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/code-security/a26/`:
- `drill-findings.json`
- `drill-review.md`
- `bu-update-authz.repro.test.ts`
